summary: The Martial Crown: the sword of the Stabilo Pact, in debt to Postondoroth, with an old seat that may lie in its own land.

morods_marshals_spirit.name: Morod's Marshals
morods_marshals_spirit.desc: The king's marshals sleep in the war-hall and eat at the king's table. They have fought each other for the post, and the survivors are not gentle.

sword_kingdom.name: The Sword Kingdom
sword_kingdom.desc: Every child in Drak knows how to hold a spear before learning a letter, and every lord holds his land by the sword. Other crowns call Drak rude, and are careful not to say so near its border.

pact_drill.name: Drilled With the Shield-Companies
pact_drill.desc: Drak's spearmen learn the shield-wall drill of Stabilo's old companies, row on row, until a company moves as one man. The drill-masters say it is the only lesson that outlasts a king.

shield_of_postondoroth.name: The Shield of Postondoroth
shield_of_postondoroth.desc: Drak's levies guard the Pact's roads from the southern watch to the Gold Road gate. Postondoroth's merchants sleep soundly because Drak's spears do not.

caravan_war_drak.name: Drak Rides for the Pact
caravan_war_drak.desc: The war-horn has sounded in Postondoroth, and Drak's riders are already on the road. They ride with their king's banner and the Pact's gold.

focuses.name: The Martial Crown
focuses.desc: King Morod holds Drak by the sword, as his fathers did before the caravan roads were opened. His crown is plain iron, and he has never thought to gild it.

focuses.name: Morod's Marshals
focuses.desc: The king gathers his marshals in the war-hall and sets a map on the table. Each is told which road he will hold and which river he will not cross.

focuses.name: The War-Halls
focuses.desc: Long halls stand in every fortress town, with drums on the walls and racks of spears below. Young men sleep there before their first campaign, and old men tell them how it ends.

focuses.name: The King's Champions
focuses.desc: Twelve champions stand at the king's right hand, picked by combat and sworn by iron. Drak's riders say a champion is worth a company, and the champions say nothing.

focuses.name: The Iron Tithe
focuses.desc: Every lord of Drak pays a tithe in iron bars, weighed in the king's hall and stacked behind the throne. A king with iron in the cellar can afford a long war.

focuses.name: The King's Hunt
focuses.desc: Each spring the king rides out with every lord, a hundred horse and three hundred hounds. The boar they kill matters less than the order they ride in.

focuses.name: The Sword Kingdom
focuses.desc: Drak is known across the East as the realm that keeps its quarrels sharp. Its neighbours leave the border alone, and the Pact leans on its blade.

focuses.name: Sword of the Pact
focuses.desc: Drak is the oldest partner of the Stabilo Pact, and its king has sworn to ride at the Pact's call. Postondoroth's treasurers speak of Drak as their sword and of Morod as its hilt.

focuses.name: Drill With the Shield-Companies
focuses.desc: Drak's levies are sent to the Pact's drill-grounds, where old shield-company captains teach the wall-and-spear. Few come home unchanged.

focuses.name: Forts Toward Furvior
focuses.desc: A line of forts rises along the northern border, facing the camel country of Noris. The garrisons are told that they are a deterrent, and are drilled as though they were not.

focuses.name: The Pact's Cavalry
focuses.desc: Drak's horse-farms supply every rider the Pact can mount, and its breeders are sent to Postondoroth to teach the stud-masters. The best colts always stay in Drak.

focuses.name: War Chest of the Pact
focuses.desc: Postondoroth lends a chest of silver against the Pact's service. Morod accepts it with a nod and signs with a heavy hand.

focuses.name: Pact Riders on the Gold Road
focuses.desc: Mounted companies patrol the Gold Road from the border to the first well. Merchants say that robbers have grown scarce, and that the riders have grown proud.

focuses.name: Ready for the Caravan War
focuses.desc: If the two great roads come to blows, Drak's riders will ride beside Stabilo's, and the king has told his marshals so in plain words. Drak will fight only as the Pact's sworn member.

focuses.name: The Shield of Postondoroth
focuses.desc: Drak's levies garrison the Pact's gates, and the standing guard at Postondoroth wears Drak's colours. The Pact's seat is safe in Drak's keeping.

focuses.name: The Old Seat
focuses.desc: Postondoroth's old halls stand in Drak's land, their windows dark and their stair worn. The king's heralds ask whether the seat should be kept, yielded or left to the dust.

effects.tooltip: Postondoroth's old halls stand in our land.

focuses.name: Yield the Old Seat
focuses.desc: Morod gives the old halls to Stabilo and lays down the claim of his fathers. The debt is struck out, the Pact's bankers bow, and Drak's old lords grumble in their cups.

focuses.name: Keep the Old Seat
focuses.desc: The old halls are swept, relit and garrisoned by Drak's guards. Stabilo's heralds call it a theft, and Drak's heralds call it a homecoming.

focuses.name: The Seat of Drak
focuses.desc: The old halls become the seat of Drak's kings, and the throne is carried in from the war-hall. A mint and a counting-house follow within the year.

focuses.name: The Debt to Postondoroth
focuses.desc: Morod owes Postondoroth's houses a sum that has grown every year since his father borrowed it. His treasurers keep the figure in a locked drawer and read it only when they must.

effects.tooltip: Drak's debt to the houses of Postondoroth is entered in the ledger.

focuses.name: Pay in Iron
focuses.desc: The king's smiths forge bars for Postondoroth's counting-house in lieu of coin. The debt falls, and so does the king's pride.

focuses.name: Borrow for the Army
focuses.desc: A larger loan is signed, and the silver is spent on spears, shields and drill-masters. Morod tells his marshals the debt is a weapon like any other.

focuses.name: Free of the Ledger
focuses.desc: The last page of the ledger is turned, and Postondoroth's clerks fold it away. Morod holds a feast in the war-hall and drinks to a debt paid.
